item.title: Witnesses or Video Sought After SUV Slams into Police Vehicle
item.dc:creator: Linda Swain
item.description:
Well, b'ys, let me tell ya about the latest bit o' excitement on the TCH. Last Wednesday, an RCMP fella had pulled someone over near Brigus Junction – probably for drivin' like they were headin' to the shed on a Friday night or something. Anyways, the copper was back in his car with the flashy lights on, mind you, when a white Hyundai Venue came along and rear-ended 'im! Boom! Knocked the squad car onto its side and into the ditch.
Both the officer and the Hyundai driver ended up in hospital, but seems they’re alright. Now the highway had to be closed, which must have gone down real well with anyone tryin' to get home in time for their supper, eh? The Mounties are sniffin’ around for videos or witnesses, so if you saw anything or got it on your fancy dash cam, give 'em a shout. Holy Lord, nothin' like a bit of drama to keep yer commute interestin'!

item.title: Fuel Prices Relatively Unchanged in Weekly Adjustment
item.dc:creator: Sara Strickland
item.description: Well, b'y, hold onto yer hat! There's barely a change in the fuel prices this week. Gas is down by a monumental half a cent—guess we’ll be swimmin' in savings, eh? Diesel’s a cent cheaper here and in Labrador West, so not exactly enough to buy a cup o' Tetley tea with. And if yer lookin' at furnace or stove oil, you’ll be penny pinchin’ with less than a cent drop. Propane’s gone down by half a cent too. Guess we all know what we'll do with all that extra coin, right? Maybe buy half a fish finger, if we're lucky. Don’t spend it all in one place!

item.title: Pharmacists Call for Expanded Coverage for Common Ailments

media:content.media:description: Dr Ashley Waghmare, PANL President (Photo via Twitter)

item.dc:creator: Beth Fagan
item.description:
Alright, b'ys, gather 'round and let me tell ya what the Pharmacy Association of Newfoundland and Labrador's on about. They're hollerin' for the gov'nment to give more people coverage for pharmacy services. Apparently, the local druggist folk have proved they ain't just good for fillin' your prescriptions – they've assessed about 30,000 folks for UTIs alone and kept 'em out of the doc's office. Can you imagine the difference that makes to a waitin' room?
Now, here's the kicker, they say they're only gettin' paid to treat eight ailments outta the 33 they're trained for. Dr. Ashley is makin' a good racket about why we need to get the other 25 covered too, includin' stuff for women's health. But y'know what? Looks like the gov'ment's got their heads buried in the sand again. They better start listenin', so we can use our pharmacists more and keep folks outta the health system queue. Honestly, if this works out, maybe next they'll pay me for tellin' tall tales down at the pub!

item.title: Busy Evening for RNC Leads to Three Arrests
item.dc:creator: Beth Fagan
item.description:
Well b'ys, the RNC had themselves a busy ol' time in St. John's yesterday, sure enough. They made three separate arrests, tackling outstanding warrants and a couple of scraps. First up, they nabbed a fella on Blackmarsh Road who was a bit too well-known to the boys in blue, given he had a few warrants out for him. Later on, the fun continued with two different fracas.
Just after 11 p.m., they were off to Military Road, collaring a 45-year-old fella who thought he could play rough and ignore his release order. Probably not the way to show you're turning a new leaf. And about the same time, over on Merrymeeting Road, a 22-year-old woman decided to join the party by allegedly throwing hands, earning herself a pair of fancy silver bracelets.
So, all three of 'em got themselves a free stay behind bars until their court appearance this morning. Must have been one wild night, eh? Maybe next time, they'll try Netflix and chillin' instead of causing a ruckus. Cheers to the RNC for keeping the streets as peaceful as a Narrows sunset!

item.title: Man Driving Flawed Pickup Charged by Harbour Grace RCMP
item.dc:creator: Sara Strickland
item.description:
Well, b'ys, you're not gonna believe this one. So, there's this young fellow from Harbour Grace, right, all of 19 years old. Cops tried to stop him 'cause his truck was in a right state, like something outta "Mad Max" – no bed on it and one headlight that's gone wonky. Instead of pulling over like a sensible human being, he decides to floor it. Smart move, eh?
The police, bless their hearts, thought better of chasing him down and let him go on his merry way for a bit, trying to avoid a scene, ya know? Turns out, he didn’t get too far. They found the truck abandoned in some gravel road mess, and got him shortly after.
Now, here's the kicker: seems like this fella was just out for a leisurely illegal drive – no license, no insurance, no nothing. Probably just popped out for a carton of milk, eh? Anyway, he's facing all kinds of charges now. Talk about going from frying pan to fire! Hope he’s got some decent yarns to spin while he's sitting on the bench. Ah, kids these days...

item.title: Trades NL Endorses PC Election Bid

media:content.media:description: Trades NL Executive Director Bob Fiander and PC Leader Tony Wakeham (VOCM News)

item.dc:creator: Linda Swain
item.description: Well b'ys, Trades NL has thrown their hat in with the PCs just in time for the October 14th election. You see, Tony Wakeham got a warm welcome at the UA Local 740 Training Centre over in Mount Pearl, with all 14 unions giving him a thumbs up. Bob Fiander, head of Trades NL, basically said the Tories are all about getting things done around here, unlike the Liberals who seem to have gone missing. They've been trying to chat with the current government for yonks, but it's the PCs who actually bothered to show up. Tony's promising all kinds of jobs, saying any work that can be done here, should be done here. Let's see if they gets her done or if it's just more talk! Personally, I'll believe it when I sees it—politicians and their promises, right? Just like trying to catch a fish with no bait sometimes!

item.title: RCMP Arrest Man After Shooting at Conne River Home
item.dc:creator: Zack Power
item.description: Oh b'y, you wouldn't believe what happened down in Conne River on the weekend. This fella, William Quinn, decided it'd be a good idea to play target practice with someone's house. Imagine that, eh? He was out there in the early hours of Sunday, givin'er with a gun on Miawpukek Drive. Lucky no one got hurt, 'cause that would've been a real b'ys ball of a situation. The Mounties nabbed him pretty quick and slapped him with charges for bein' a right clueless eejit with a firearm. I guess he figured it was Newfoundland's version of cowboy night or somethin'. Honestly, some people... What do ya think this is, the wild west?

item.title: Pet Owners Advocacy Group Demands HST Be Removed from Vet Bills
item.dc:creator: Zack Power
item.description:
Oh b'y, here's what's on the go here. You've got this bunch called the PetOwners Collective, and they’re basically trying to make vet bills a little less of a heart attack waiting to happen. They're asking the politicians to ax the provincial tax from vet bills. You know, 'cause apparently, keeping ol' Rover alive is getting dearer than a feed of lobster.
They're also saying these vet clinics could use a break on buying their top-dollar equipment. Mike Keough, who's leading the charge, reckons that some folks are having to think twice about looking after their critters 'cause of the sky-high prices. I mean, someone got billed thirty grand for surgery! Sure, it’s nice insurance covered most of it, but with the taxes, yer still lookin' at over seven grand out of pocket. That's a gut-punch alright; you’d need more than a screech-in to numb that pain.
Keough also points out that pet owners are already forking over enough dough with all the pet supplies, so why not cut 'em some slack, eh? Honestly, if this keeps up, owning a pet might need its own insurance, just like a bay boat in iceberg alley.

item.title: Off-Road Vehicle Ban Lifted Tonight
item.dc:creator: Linda Swain
item.description: Oh, b'ys, listen ta this: the government decided ta lift the ban on off-road vehicles in the woods, since the rain's been comin' in and the temperatures have cooled off a bit. So, come midnight, we can fire up the ATVs again, but don't lose yer minds just yet. They're sayin' we still gotta be careful about what's around us and make sure yer cartin' around a fire extinguisher. Wouldn't it be a grand time gettin' yer ATV stuck in the bog, tryin' to put out a fire, eh? Anyways, the ban's s'posed to get another look at on September 7th. So, go on, enjoy the ride but keep 'er between the ditches, eh?

item.title: Local Business Devastated by Fire, Offering Help to Others

media:content.media:description: Salty Sea Cottages in Ochre Pit Cove (via Facebook)

item.dc:creator: Linda Swain
item.description:
Well, b'ys, there's been a right old kerfuffle down in Ochre Pit Cove, let me tell ya. The folks at Salty Seas Cottages have taken quite the hit. Three of their cottages went up in smoke, along with their big ol' storage shed – and one of those cottages was a grand ol’ place over a hundred years old, practically like losing a family member if you ask me.
Two of them cottages had just flung open their doors for Canada Day, would ya believe? Timing ain't always on your side, eh? But fair play to 'em, they're still trying to lend a hand by offering up the cottages that didn’t go up in flames for anyone out by the b'y who needs a roof over their head. That's what we do around here, right? Look out for each other, even when ya got troubles of your own.
Mind you, who knows what's left of six more cottages and a craft store, since they've not had a chance to check 'em out yet. Let's hope those flaming fires give it a rest, and they can get back on their feet soon enough! Bit of a crock, but what can ya do? Onwards and upwards, I s'pose!
